verified.note: Table I, row 'HH model (g^2/w = 1.0)', column CS-HF (line 840); version read: arXiv text (sources/2310.13084.txt, v2 per the 2026-11-24 worklist) with the authors' code (github.com/zhcui/polar_preview, example/00-holstein_model.py); the journal version was not read | Sec. II A, Eqs. (1)-(4) of the arXiv text (lines 95-111): H = sum h_pq a+_p a_q + (1/2) sum V a+a+aa + sum_x w_x b+_x b_x + sum_x sum_pq g_xpq a+_p a_q (b+_x + b_x), no zero-point term; Hubbard-Holstein: h_pq = t on nearest neighbours, V = U delta..., w_x = w, g_xpq = g delta_xp delta_pq, so the coupling is g n_p (b+_p + b_p) and the instance's g is the printed g. Table I labels the coupling g^2/w (= 1.0 and 2.4) at w = 0.5: g = sqrt(1.0 x 0.5) = sqrt(0.5) and sqrt(2.4 x 0.5) = sqrt(1.2) (arithmetic on printed numbers). One electron, so U drops out and the instance is Holstein f1. Implied, not stated (RULES.md 8): (1) the lattice is 4 sites with periodic closure, and (2) t = 1, which gives the unit of energy; Table I prints neither. Evidence: Sec. III A (line 344) 'we consider a single electron on a 4-site Hubbard-Holstein model with different phonon frequencies (w) and coupling strengths (g^2/w)'; Fig. 2 caption (line 439): 'The periodic lattice size L is taken as 4. (b) w = 0.5, one electron'; Table I caption (lines 831-837): HH models (w = 0.5) with one electron; Table I g^2/w = 2.4 is the value Fig. 2 marks at the self-trapping transition (lines 441, 447). The code the paper cites (Code availability, Ref. [57] = github.com/zhcui/polar_preview, single commit cf180fb, cloned and read 2026-11-26), example/00-holstein_model.py, builds exactly this model: nao = 4, nelec = 1, U = 0, hcore[i, i+1] = -1.0 and hcore[nao-1, 0] = hcore[0, nao-1] = -1.0 (# PBC), w_p = 0.5, g = sqrt(alpha w_p) with alpha = g^2/w on the grid 0.0 to 3.0 in steps of 0.2 (which contains 1.0 and 2.4), coupling h_ep[x, x, x] = g. So |t| = 1; on a 4-site ring the spectrum is the same for t = +1 and -1 (bipartite). Only this reading agrees with the printed code. Bound type: CS-HF is the energy of a single-determinant coherent-state product wave function with optimised shifts; LF-HF, uniform LF-HF and GLF-HF are the energies of Lang-Firsov-transformed single determinants with variationally optimised parameters ('we call this the variational LF-HF', Sec. II C; 'variationally optimize the transformation parameters', abstract). Each is the expectation value of H in a state, so variational. arXiv text only: the ACS PDF was not reachable (HTTP 403 in the 2026-11-24 worklist), so the row is admissible but not fully verified (RULES.md 8) and must be read again against the journal version.
